summary: A server-side proxy and cache serving whole-table rate proposals from whitelisted keyless providers, plus the operator's symbol table, which the account form's unit picker is built from and an administrator maintains.

read.role: GET /api/rates/symbols is a vault route and every /api/admin/symbols route is an administration route, each Not Found to the other kind. Configuration names the variables for the limit and for the failure count and cool-off of each provider's breaker, and Database the attempts table the limit's rows live in and their pruning
the consumer of a proposal and the reason the client never names a symbol. Reading defines a rate source at a date from the table's lookup and since, which is why since is on the wire
an account's unit is its rate symbol, which is what the table is a picker for
the kind: currency rows are the whole of the main-currency list
the boundary the symbol table clears without an exception

the oracle for every proposal (known_table applies the composition pinned in Providers), the trust-store route by which the harness reaches the app's provider hosts without any setting, and the module-level names sources.py imports from solvent.rates (moduleConstants). The harness is built against this feature, not the reverse
the combobox, chip, table and section-switcher conventions the unit picker and the admin Units screen use, and the phone-width sizes

sections: What it deliberately does not show
The rates, at the foot of the sweep
Rate lines on a reopened recording
read.role: where a proposal is shown, accepted, overridden or reported missing
the unit picker built from this table

endpoint.value: GET /api/rates?date=<YYYY-MM-DD>&quote=<CCY>[&symbol=<SYMBOL>]. Session-authenticated, and anonymous requests are refused so the proxy is not an open relay

acceptedParameterSet.value: exactly {symbol, date, quote}, with symbol the only optional one. Any request carrying an unrecognised query parameter is rejected with Bad Request rather than ignored, which is the base-amount rule made structural: there is no field an amount could travel in

singleSymbolResponse.value: { rate, base, quote, asOf, source, cached }

wholeTableResponse.value: { date, quote, rates: { <symbol>: { rate, base, asOf, source, cached } } }. A symbol the proxy cannot price for that date is absent from the map, never present with a null

clientNeverNamesASymbol.value: every request the app makes omits symbol. The single-symbol form stays because the acceptance sweep queries every symbol in the table individually, which is what keeps /api/rates/symbols and /api/rates from drifting apart

noEditedRateIsEverSent.value: a price the person typed or overrode is never sent to this endpoint, in any field

symbolTableEndpoint.value: GET /api/rates/symbols returning [{ symbol, label, kind, lookup, since }], session-authenticated, read-only, cacheable, and omitting retired rows. The admin list GET /api/admin/symbols does not carry since

symbolSince.value: since is the symbol's floor, YYYY-MM-DD, or null for a symbol with no provider adapter. It does not follow lookup: the floor is the provider's fact, so a currency whose lookup an administrator turned off keeps its date, and a main currency whose lookup is off still bounds every rate quoted into it. The client computes a rate source at a date from it with no request (record-rate.json, rateSourceAtADate)

symbolFloor.value: a symbol's floor is the first date its provider publishes it: 1999-01-04 for Frankfurter, 2013-01-02 for NBP, raised for a currency whose series begins later (currencyFloorsLater). A symbol with no provider adapter has no floor. The floor is a server-side constant derived from the adapter registry like hasAdapter, never stored on the row and never set through any route, and it holds whatever the row's lookup. A currency an administrator adds takes 1999-01-04, because the server knows no later start for it

adminListCarriesNoSince.value: GET /api/admin/symbols carries no since, because no administrator decision turns on it: lookup is refused only for want of an adapter

lookupOffWithAnAdapter.value: a symbol with an adapter and lookup turned off answers Bad Request before its floor, like any symbol with that floor. On or after its floor it answers No Content with no outbound request and no error log. A symbol with no adapter has no floor and answers No Content at every date

currencyFloorsLater.condition: before 2000-01-13 the Frankfurter table omits those four, and a request with one of them as base answers Not Found, which would count against Frankfurter's breaker

rateSourceFromDate.value: a rate source applies to a date only on or after the later of the symbol's floor and the quote's. Before that date no provider is asked, which is a designed state like lookup: false and never an outage

symbolKind.value: currency or metal. Display and grouping only

symbolLookupFlag.value: whether the proxy can price this symbol today. false means valid and canonical with no provider yet: the user enters the rate by hand and /api/rates answers No Content, not Bad Request, except before the floor of a symbol that has an adapter (lookupOffWithAnAdapter). A designed state, not a degraded one

list.value: GET /api/admin/symbols returning the full table including retired rows, each carrying symbol, label, kind, lookup, retired and hasAdapter

create.value: POST /api/admin/symbols { symbol, label, kind, lookup }. symbol must match the canonical form and not already exist

patch.value: PATCH /api/admin/symbols/<symbol> { label?, lookup?, retired? }, changing only those three

hasAdapter.value: whether this deployment has a provider adapter configured for that symbol. Derived from the adapter registry rather than stored on the row, read-only, and POST and PATCH reject it like any other unknown field. It is what lets the screen disable the lookup control on rows with no source instead of explaining a refusal afterwards, and the server keeps refusing regardless, because a client's knowledge of the registry is not a control

symbolImmutability.value: symbol and kind are immutable and there is no delete route, because a symbol is written into user records as an account's unit inside ciphertext the server cannot read. retired: true is the substitute for deleting: the row is dropped from GET /api/rates/symbols so no new account can be measured in it, and stays fully valid everywhere else

lookupTrueRequiresAnAdapter.value: the server refuses lookup: true for a symbol with no configured provider adapter, on POST and on PATCH alike

noUsageCounts.value: no response here counts how many accounts use a symbol, and none could, because the server cannot read a unit

labelRendering.value: label is display text, changes freely, is stored in no user record, and is rendered into the unit picker with textContent and never innerHTML

seededMetalSymbols.value: XAU-ozt Gold troy ounce metal lookup yes, XAU-g Gold gram metal lookup yes, XAG-ozt Silver troy ounce metal lookup no, XAG-g Silver gram metal lookup no, XPT-ozt Platinum troy ounce metal lookup no, XPT-g Platinum gram metal lookup no, XPD-ozt Palladium troy ounce metal lookup no, XPD-g Palladium gram metal lookup no

symbolNamingRule.value: <ISO 4217 metal code>-<unit>, unit ozt or g, so a future symbol is derivable rather than invented

seededCurrencySymbols.value: seeded from Frankfurter's own currency list, all with lookup: true. There are no security symbols and none are coming

fxProvider.value: Frankfurter's public instance, api.frankfurter.dev. HTTPS, no API key, no quota. An FX symbol is the base currency code and quote is the user's main currency

goldProvider.value: Narodowy Bank Polski's public API, api.nbp.pl, HTTPS, no API key. Lookup is a range query GET /api/cenyzlota/{date-14d}/{date}, taking the last entry on or before date. An empty result inside the window is No Content, and the API caps a range at 93 days

goldQuoteConversion.value: NBP prices in PLN only, so a non-PLN quote converts PLN to quote through Frankfurter at the asOf date, not the requested date. Either leg failing yields No Content, and a half-composed rate is never returned. source names the chain, nbp+frankfurter, or nbp when the quote is PLN

goldUnitConversion.value: XAU-g takes NBP's figure directly and XAU-ozt multiplies by 31.1034768. Compose in this order and round once, at the end: cena x (1 / rates["PLN"]) from the asOf table (cena alone when the quote is PLN), then x 31.1034768 for XAU-ozt, then the rounding in proposalComposition

proposalComposition.value: every proposal is composed in Decimal at the default context's 28 significant digits and rounded once, to 8 decimal places, half to even, written as a plain decimal string with no trailing zeros and no exponent. The steps before that rounding are pinned per provider so an independent computation in the same order reaches the same digits

fxRead.value: from the Frankfurter body the app reads base (must equal quote), date (the publication day, which becomes asOf) and rates (how many of each code one quote buys). The price of one unit of a code is 1 / rates[code]. Nothing else in the body is read

value.NBP_URL: https://api.nbp.pl/api/cenyzlota/{start}/{end}?format=json, start 14 days before date and end equal to it

noSettingNamesAProvider.value: no environment variable, configuration value, command-line flag or request names a provider host, a URL template or a certificate authority. Verification runs against the image's system trust store at OpenSSL's default paths and the app adds no CA of its own. A proxy in https_proxy, which urllib honours, can carry a connection and cannot change where it ends, because the certificate is still verified against the provider's own name

environmentVariablesRead.value: exactly those app-shell.md Configuration names and the proxy variables urllib reads, and none of them changes the outbound URL or the TLS context

moduleConstants.condition: solvent.rates exposes these under exactly those names because the nightly source check imports them. Renaming one breaks that check. EGRESS_TIMEOUT_SECONDS covers connect and read together across one proxy request

goldAsOfLag.value: NBP's price trails the London fixing by one business day, so asOf is usually one business day behind the requested date even midweek. Do not paper over it by stamping asOf with the requested date

cache.value: key (symbol, quote, date), stored in SQLite. Past dates cached indefinitely, today's date cached for 1 hour then refetched. A cache hit issues no outbound request. Entries are public reference data, not per-user, and hold nothing about who asked

symbolValidation.value: symbol must match ^(?=.{1,16}$)[A-Z0-9][A-Z0-9._]*(-[a-z]+)?$, an upper-case code and an optional lower-case unit, and be present in the server's configured symbol table. Regex alone is not sufficient

quoteValidation.value: quote must be a kind: currency row of the server's symbol table, not merely a known ISO 4217 code

dateValidation.value: date must parse as a calendar date and not be in the future. For a symbol with a provider adapter, whatever its lookup, it must not precede the later of the symbol's floor and the quote's (symbolFloor): 2013-01-02 for gold, 1999-01-04 for a currency, 2000-01-13 for BRL, CNY, ILS and INR, each provider's own history start. A date before it is a Bad Request and reaches no provider. A single global floor is wrong in both directions

wholeTableBeforeAFloor.value: the whole-table form leaves out every symbol whose floor (the later of its own and the quote's) the date precedes and asks no provider for it. When every symbol is out, the answer is No Content with no outbound request and no change to any breaker's count. It is never a Bad Request, which the single-symbol form returns for the same date

fxFloor.value: 1999-01-04 for the ECB series the /v1 endpoints the app calls serve, 2000-01-13 for BRL, CNY, ILS and INR (currencyFloorsLater). Frankfurter's advertised history back to 1948 comes from other series and is not the API the app calls

egressHardening.value: provider hosts and URL templates are server-side constants with no part of the outbound URL derived from client input, redirects are disabled rather than followed to a validated target, egress has a hard timeout of 5 seconds connect plus read across one proxy request, shared by that request's providers as outboundScheduling pins, and a response size cap, requests go to HTTPS only with certificate verification on, and no provider API key appears in any response, log line or error message (no provider in this design has one, and the rule binds a keyed provider added later)

perUserRateLimit.value: default 120 per hour on the endpoint, independent of the login limiter. Operator config with that default, variable RATE_REQUESTS_PER_HOUR. A sweep of any size costs one request, so the limit sits far above honest use

perUserRateLimitRows.value: one request row in the bucket rates:<principal id> per lookup let through, deleted once older than 60 minutes. A refused request writes no row, in this limiter as in every other, so the limit lifts an hour after the oldest lookup it let through, however often the client retried

circuitBreaker.value: one breaker per provider, keyed frankfurter and nbp. A breaker opens after 5 consecutive failures of its own provider and for a 5-minute cool-off fails that provider's requests without sending them, instead of retrying per request, so every symbol needing that provider gets no proposal. Operator config with those defaults, variables RATE_BREAKER_FAILURES and RATE_BREAKER_COOLOFF_MINUTES, whose failure count and cool-off apply to each breaker alike

breakerFailureDefinition.value: an outbound request that cannot connect, times out, answers anything but 200, or answers a body that is not JSON. A success resets its own provider's count and touches no other breaker

breakerGoldFxLeg.value: the gold lookup's currency leg is a Frankfurter request and counts against Frankfurter's breaker, never NBP's. While Frankfurter is down NBP requests still go out and gold quoted in PLN still resolves. While NBP is down every currency lookup still goes out

noSharedBreaker.value: there is no breaker shared by both providers, because one provider's outage would silence the other and the other's successes would keep resetting the count

outboundSelection.value: a proxy request sends only the outbound requests its pending symbols need, a pending symbol being one neither cached nor the identity case. Frankfurter's table for date goes out when a currency symbol is pending, NBP's range query when a gold symbol is, and the gold quote leg only for a gold symbol quoted in anything but PLN

outboundScheduling.value: Frankfurter's table and NBP's range query go out at once, and the proxy request waits for both within its one EGRESS_TIMEOUT_SECONDS deadline, so a hanging provider cannot use up the deadline before the other is asked. The deadline is not split into a share per provider, because that cuts the time each gets and fails a slow provider that would answer within it. The gold quote leg goes out once NBP has answered, because it is fetched at NBP's asOf, and has only what is left of the deadline. When asOf is the requested date and the table for date is already going out, the leg waits for that request instead of sending a second one

outboundThreads.value: outbound requests run on threads of their own, each handed its provider, URL and deadline as values. They touch no database connection and no Flask context: caching and composing the response happen on the request's thread once every outbound request has returned. A breaker's count changes under a lock, because the table and the quote leg can be in flight to Frankfurter at once

hangBound.value: a whole-table request returns within EGRESS_TIMEOUT_SECONDS plus one second when a provider hangs, both or either. A stub that hangs accepts the connection and sends nothing until after the deadline, so the client's own timeout ends the wait

breakerLivesInProcessMemory.value: the breakers live in process memory, so the nightly harness's app_stop and app_start reset every one

noProposalAvailable.condition: a symbol with no provider yet, no data for that date, a provider unreachable, a lookup: false symbol on or after its floor, a symbol with no adapter at any date, a failed FX leg on gold, or a whole-table request where every symbol failed or was left out by a floor. Never an error (spec/features/rate-lookup.md#edge-cases)

identityRate.condition: symbol equals quote answers rate '1', base naming that unit, asOf the requested date, source 'identity', cached false, and no outbound request (spec/features/rate-lookup.md#edge-cases)

unknownSymbolOrParameter.condition: a symbol absent from the table, an unrecognised query parameter, a future date, or a date below the floor of a symbol with an adapter (lookup off included) or below the quote's, in the single-symbol form (spec/features/rate-lookup.md#edge-cases)

overPerUserLimit.condition: and no attempts row is written (spec/features/rate-lookup.md#acceptance-criteria)

unauthenticated.condition: and no outbound request is made (spec/features/rate-lookup.md#acceptance-criteria)

wrongSurface.condition: every /api/admin/symbols route to a vault owner, and GET /api/rates/symbols to an administrator (spec/features/rate-lookup.md#acceptance-criteria)

fixtures: a stubbed FX provider and a stubbed NBP that can each be made to hang, fail, redirect toward an internal address, return a zero or non-numeric rate, return a rate in an unexpected currency, and publish nothing for a requested Saturday
an NBP stub with nothing published across the whole 14-day window, for the No Content case
an FX stub returning a different rate per date, for the assertion that the gold quote leg is fetched at asOf rather than at the requested date
the adapter registry itself, read at test time, for the hasAdapter assertion, rather than a fixture listing which symbols have adapters
a route enumerator over the registered routes, for the assertion that no route deletes a symbol
a seeded administrator session and a seeded vault owner session, for the two Not Found directions
a quote that is a valid ISO 4217 code the FX provider does not serve, which is the case a plain ISO check waves through
a fifteen-account, six-symbol vault, for the one-request sweep assertion
a stubbed clock and the attempts table readable row for row, for the refused-request-writes-no-row and lifts-an-hour-after-the-oldest assertions
a stubbed opener recording every outbound request, for an FX table, gold quoted in PLN and gold quoted in CHF, for the URL-and-headers assertion

a stub publishing rates["USD"] = 1.0876 and rates["PLN"] = 4.2537 against CHF and cena = 251.37, for the digit-for-digit composition assertion (USD 0.91945568, and XAU-g and XAU-ozt from cena x (1 / 4.2537), the latter times 31.1034768, rounded half-even to 8 places)
a recorder over every read of os.environ through start-up and a whole-table lookup, for the environment-variable assertion

the stubbed clock and the stubbed opener driving each provider independently: Frankfurter failing while NBP answers and the reverse, with a different date per request so no cache entry answers in place of the provider, and failures of each kind (cannot connect, timeout, non-200, non-JSON body)
whole-table requests quoted in PLN, for the case where gold needs no Frankfurter leg, and quoted in CHF, for the gold FX leg counted against Frankfurter

a stub provider that hangs: it accepts the connection and sends nothing until after the deadline, so the app's own timeout ends the wait. Settable per provider, for both hanging, Frankfurter hanging with NBP answering, and NBP hanging with Frankfurter answering

a stubbed opener that records each outbound request with the time it was sent, for the assertions that the two providers' first requests go out together and that the quote leg for an asOf equal to the requested date sends nothing a second time
the whole symbol table read from GET /api/rates/symbols, with a currency an administrator turned lookup off for, for the since sweep: it keeps its date, and null belongs to a symbol with no adapter

a stubbed Frankfurter that answers Not Found for BRL, CNY, ILS and INR as base before 2000-01-13 and omits them from the table, with Frankfurter's failure count readable, for the quote-floor assertions dated 1999-06-30 quoted in CHF and in BRL
focus: the accepted parameter set must be enumerated and asserted to be exactly {symbol, date, quote}. This is the structural form of the base-amount rule, and a handler that simply ignores extra parameters passes every functional test while leaving a field an amount could travel in
hasAdapter must be asserted against the adapter registry itself rather than against a fixture, so the two cannot drift, and every symbol carrying lookup: true must also carry hasAdapter: true
the absence of a delete route must be asserted by enumerating the registered routes, not by checking that a guessed path returns Not Found
the gold quote leg must be fetched at the asOf date, asserted against a stub that returns a different rate for each date. Both orders produce a plausible number and only this stub tells them apart

the SSRF assertions need the provider stubbed to reply with a redirect toward an internal address, and the test has to confirm no request to that address was made, not merely that the response was an error

GET /api/rates/symbols must be swept: query every returned symbol at /api/rates and assert none is a Bad Request, with lookup: false symbols included and answering No Content. This is what keeps the two endpoints from drifting, and it is the assertion nobody writes by hand
the whole-table and single-symbol forms must be shown to share one cache, by following a table request with a single-symbol request and asserting no second outbound request
a fifteen-row sweep across six symbols must issue exactly one request here, asserted as a count. Every data assertion passes under a per-symbol fan-out

no /api/admin/symbols response may carry a count, list or any other indication of which accounts use a symbol, asserted against the full response shape rather than against the fields the screen happens to read

exceeding the per-user limit must be shown to write no attempts row: retry repeatedly while over it, compare the table row for row, and show the limit lifting an hour after the oldest lookup it let through. A limiter that records each refused request extends the throttle with every retry and never lifts

the per-symbol floors must be asserted on both sides for both classes: a currency on 1998-12-31 is a Bad Request that reaches no provider and on 1999-01-04 is priced, and gold on 2012-12-31 is a Bad Request and on 2013-01-02 is priced. One global floor passes either pair alone

the composition must be asserted digit for digit against an independent Decimal computation in the pinned order, not by approximate equality. Rounding at an intermediate step, or computing the ounce figure as cena x 31.1034768 before the PLN leg, gives a plausible number that differs in the last places

the outbound URL and both headers must be asserted against the stubbed opener for all three request shapes. A test that only checks the response passes with a wrong host, a missing Accept or an unnamed User-Agent that the real CDN would refuse

the environment assertion must record every read of os.environ through start-up and a whole-table lookup and compare the set to the Configuration names plus the proxy variables. A grep of the source passes while a setting that names a provider hides in a helper

the breakers must be asserted per provider, each request on a different date so the cache cannot answer. With Frankfurter failing and NBP answering, PLN-quoted whole-table requests must still send their NBP request and return the gold symbols while Frankfurter's breaker opens on the configured Frankfurter failure and no Frankfurter request goes out inside the cool-off. With NBP failing past the count, currency rates must still come back and only the gold symbols be absent. A single shared breaker passes the first-opens-then-skips check for either provider alone and fails only this pair

NBP successes interleaved with Frankfurter failures must not reset Frankfurter's count, asserted by the breaker opening on exactly the configured Frankfurter failure and not later. A shared count reset by any success passes every test that fails one provider at a time

a failing FX leg of a gold request must be shown to count against Frankfurter's breaker and not NBP's, by reading how many requests each provider then receives. Counting it against the provider the request was routed to passes a test that looks only at the response
each provider must be shown to be asked again once its own cool-off has passed, and the other left untouched meanwhile, using the stubbed clock rather than a sleep

the hang criteria must be asserted with a stub that really hangs, timed against EGRESS_TIMEOUT_SECONDS plus one second, in all three combinations: both hanging gives No Content, Frankfurter hanging gives the gold symbols and no currency rate in a PLN-quoted request, NBP hanging gives the currency rates and no gold symbols. A stub that errors at once passes all three while the requests are still asked one after the other, which is what the criteria exist to rule out

a request must be shown to send only what its pending symbols need: a table of only currency symbols sends no NBP request, a table of only gold symbols sends no Frankfurter table, and a gold symbol quoted in PLN sends no quote leg. Asserted against the recorded outbound requests, not the response

the quote leg must be shown to wait for NBP and to reuse the in-flight table when asOf is the requested date and a currency symbol is pending, asserted by counting Frankfurter requests, which is one rather than two

the outbound threads must be shown to touch no database connection and no Flask context, with caching and composing done on the request's thread, and a breaker's count to survive the table and the quote leg failing at once without a lost update. A count changed without the lock passes every sequential test

the provider API key rule has to be checked against a real log line, response body and error page, even though no provider in this design has a key. The rule exists to bind a keyed provider added later

since must be asserted over the whole table against the server's floors: 1999-01-04 for USD, 2000-01-13 for BRL, 2013-01-02 for XAU-g and XAU-ozt, null for XAG-ozt only, a currency whose lookup was turned off keeping its date. For every row but EUR with a since, a single-symbol request quoted in EUR dated the day before it must be a Bad Request with no outbound request, and one dated since itself must send its outbound request when the row's lookup is on and answer No Content with none when it is off, so since and the floor cannot drift

the quote's floor must be asserted separately from the symbol's: a whole-table request dated 1999-06-30 quoted in CHF returns USD with BRL, CNY, ILS and INR absent, and quoted in BRL sends no outbound request, answers No Content and leaves Frankfurter's failure count where it was. A server that checks only the symbol's floor sends Frankfurter a base it answers Not Found for and opens its breaker on a request nobody should have made

a symbol with no adapter must be shown to answer No Content with no outbound request at 2012-12-31 and at 1998-12-31 (XAG-ozt), while gold on 2012-12-31 in the single-symbol form is a Bad Request. A currency with an adapter and lookup turned off must answer Bad Request before its floor and No Content from it, because the floor follows the adapter and not the flag. Giving every symbol the gold or the currency floor, or tying the floor to lookup, passes one case and fails another

a whole-table request dated 2012-12-31 quoted in CHF must send Frankfurter's request and no NBP request and return the currencies with both gold symbols absent. A date check applied to the request as a whole rejects it or sends NBP's query for a date NBP has nothing for
